home.labDesc: Drag reagents into a beaker and let the reaction engine detect color changes, bubbles, precipitates, and temperature shifts in real time — what you see is what you get.

quant.verdictGood: Data consistency is good — suitable for calculation
quant.verdictFair: Deviation is high; check line of sight when reading and verify system stability
quant.verdictPoor: Deviation is too large; identify the cause before repeating parallel measurements
quant.singleReading: Only 1 measurement — relative deviation cannot be calculated (protocol requires at least 2 parallel measurements)
quant.groupNote: A new group is created each time the system is sampled, mixed, or heated. Readings across groups do not constitute parallel measurements and are therefore tallied separately.
quant.noReadings: No measurement records were captured using the “Read” operation in this experiment, so mean and relative deviation cannot be calculated. Quantitative experiments require at least 2 repeated readings under the same system state.

stir.label: Stir
stir.effect: Stir with a glass stirring rod to speed up solute dissolution and improve mixing
stir.hint: Stirring accelerates dissolving and heat transfer, and equalizes local concentration so readings represent the bulk solution

shake.label: Shake
shake.effect: Shake to mix thoroughly and ensure full contact between reagents
shake.hint: With small volumes in a test tube, shaking (not stirring) is used to mix — keep the mouth of the tube pointed away from people

heat.label: Heat
heat.effect: Light the alcohol lamp to heat the system and raise its temperature
heat.hint: Most reactions speed up with heat; endothermic reactions require continuous heating to proceed

cool.label: Cool
cool.effect: Remove the heat source and allow the system to cool naturally
cool.hint: Cooling reduces solubility — a standard step for crystallization and product collection

settle.label: Settle
settle.effect: Allow to stand briefly so precipitates sink and liquid layers separate more clearly
settle.hint: Precipitation and phase separation take time; only after settling can you judge whether the supernatant is clear

read.label: Read
read.hint: Read with your eye level with the graduation mark; log each reading in the data table to calculate averages and errors

electrolysisLab.depleted: Cu²⁺ in solution is nearly exhausted. Continued electrolysis would cause hydrogen gas evolution at the cathode. Power has been cut automatically.
